title: SUSTAINED FIRE PINS A PILLAGER
why: His yes to suggestion 22, suppression, as a pillager behaviour. Rounds of yours that go past a hostile pillager count against him; four of them inside under two seconds pin him for about two and a half seconds, and more fire keeps him pinned. A pinned pillager stops advancing and stops flanking, ducks down, slips behind cover if there is cover that is no nearer to you, and what he shoots is wild. So the rate of fire matters: a Support MG pins a man in about half a second, a Magnum or a Marksman Rifle seldom does. A round from player 2 that lands on a man counts the same, and player 2 sees him duck. Pillagers you are not shooting at behave exactly as before.
now: Heavy fire near a pillager now pins him: he ducks, stops advancing and shoots wild.
